Subject: FintechCo - logging & redaction (post-demo recap / next steps)

Thanks again for the demo time today, Alex — appreciate the context on your production troubleshooting flow. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: Give FintechCo the ability to diagnose production issues while ensuring no PII persists in logs and all retained telemetry for EU traffic stays in-region.
- Key asks from you: whether you need full request/response bodies (no), whether trace IDs are required for troubleshooting (yes), retention window target, and any header types you consider sensitive.

Notes / clarifying questions for you:
1) Trace IDs: do you need the raw trace ID value in our logs, or would a hashed/opaque identifier suffice if it preserves the ability to join traces across systems?
2) Retention: do you have a target retention window for request-level logs (e.g., 30 / 90 / 180 days)?
3) Residency: confirm EU-only residency for logs generated from EU customers.
4) Headers: which headers must be stripped from request/response logs (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie typically; any others?)

Attached a short diagram showing the logging control knobs we discussed (ingest-time redaction, header allowlist/blocklist, trace-id hashing, and per-region retention).

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: confirm answers to questions above (1-4) and share any compliance checklist items.
- Redwood: we’ll propose a concrete logging configuration and timeline for a test rollout.
- Tentative follow-up call: Mon 11/9 10:00am CET — are you available?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fintechco.com>

Date: 2026-11-06T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo - logging & redaction (post-demo recap / next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Answers inline below: 

1) Trace IDs: we need a stable identifier to correlate logs with our internal traces. A hashed trace ID that is deterministic (same input => same hash) would work for correlation, as long as we can map it back on our side using the original trace passed in the request headers. We do not want raw user identifiers or raw tokens stored.

2) Retention: targeting 90 days for request-level logs should be fine; we can keep higher-level metrics longer.

3) Residency: yes — EU-only residency for logs coming from EU customers. We will provide a list of IP ranges / regions if helpful.

4) Headers: please strip Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie. Also remove any x-user-email or x-user-id headers. If you can provide an allowlist approach (only log headers we explicitly keep), that would be ideal.

Additional: For troubleshooting we sometimes need request/response metadata (status codes, latencies, model id, prompt length) — that is okay. Full request/response bodies are not required and should be redacted.

I’ll also attach our security contact (Ben) to keep the thread on the procurement/compliance side.

Availability: Mon 11/9 10:00am CET works for me.

—Alex
VP, Engineering
FintechCo
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo - logging & redaction (proposal draft)

Marissa / Steph — looping in a quick proposal we can send to Alex that maps to his answers. High-level approach we recommend: 

- Ingest-time redaction pipeline: configurable regex-based redaction rules per tenant/route (example: mask emails with /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/ => "[REDACTED_EMAIL]").
- Headers allowlist: default deny; customers define header allowlist (we will automatically drop Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, x-user-id, x-user-email unless explicitly allowed).
- Trace IDs: keep a deterministic SHA-256 truncated hash of trace-id header (e.g., sha256(trace_id)[:16]) to allow correlation without storing raw IDs. Store original trace-id only if customer requests and signs off.
- Request/response bodies: by default do not persist bodies. Provide an opt-in mechanism for short-lived inspection (ephemeral session with strict retention and audit logs).
- Retention & residency: support per-tenant retention windows; implement region-based storage buckets (EU customers -> EU-only buckets). Retention enforcement via lifecycle policies.

I attached a one-pager we can share: redaction-controls-proposal.pdf.

Action items for next touch:
- Produce an example logging policy YAML for FintechCo that implements: 90d retention, EU-only storage, header allowlist limited to [x-request-id, content-type], trace-id hashing enabled, ingest-time email masking.
- Coordinate with infra to confirm EU bucket readiness and audit logging for access to logs.
- Prep a short demo of redaction rules on synthetic examples so Alex can validate masking.

Marissa — I drafted the example policy and the demo steps; happy to take point on the demo.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: FintechCo - logging & redaction (confirming next steps)

Alex — thanks for the quick responses and Ben for joining. Per Rishi’s proposal, here are concrete next steps and owners: 

1) Redwood to deliver: example logging policy (YAML), short demo of ingest-time redaction using synthetic examples, and proposed timeline for test rollout — owner: Rishi — ETA: 2026-11-09 (demo during the 10:00am CET call).
2) FintechCo to confirm: header allowlist (we will default to deny), and provide any additional sensitive header names or patterns to be redacted — owner: Alex/Ben — ETA: 2026-11-08 EOD.
3) Compliance: Ben to share any specific procurement/security checklist items we should pre-populate before the pilot.

Operational constraints we’ve captured: 90-day request-log retention, deterministic trace-id hashing for correlation, EU-only storage for EU traffic, default deny headers, and no persistence of request/response bodies unless explicitly opted-in with audit controls.

If that matches your expectations, we’ll send the example policy and demo invite for Mon 11/9 10:00am CET. Please confirm and we’ll send calendar invitation + demo link.
